subject: ventures/photos-import-tools
professional: a digital asset manager / photo-library technician who ingests camera cards into Apple Photos for working photographers, checking first: that 'imported' means the bytes are actually in the library (not a filename match), that an interrupted or timed-out import never re-sends with duplicate detection off, that nothing reports complete while files were skipped, and that card verification covers every file the camera writes before the card is reformatted

checks.method: another tool: coreutils sha256sum on the source file
checks.command: python3 -I /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/8c3dc66b-507d-5286-a066-00cfdd39a8bd/scratchpad/photos-import-tools/probes3.py  (rsync absent in the container; rsync_copy stubbed with shutil.copytree, verify_and_manifest is the shipped code)

checks.observed: H3 size-mode errors []; hash-mode ['Hash mismatch: DCIM/100MSDCF/DSC00001.ARW']

checks.method: hand from the stated rule min(2**min(a,6),120) and sum(min(2**a,30), a=1..6)

checks.method: practice: a filename is not identity; the file must be sent to Photos (or matched by content/date) before it counts as imported

checks.observed: R1 files sent ['DSC00001','DSC00003']; exit 0; 'Complete: total=3 imported=3' -- DSC00002 marked imported without ever being imported (bulk_preflight runs on every run, not only with --photos-preflight)

checks.what: Crash / watchdog kill while a file is mid-import, then resume
checks.method: Photos AppleScript dictionary: 'import ... skip check duplicates true' disables Photos' own duplicate detection; a file whose import may already have landed must be retried with it on
checks.expected: skip check duplicates false on the retry
checks.observed: R4 'import {POSIX file ".../IMG_5.JPG"} skip check duplicates true' (recover_importing resets to 'pending', and 'pending' means duplicate check off)

checks.what: Photos.app timeout, then the worker restarts (watchdog restart or manual re-run)
checks.method: same rule: a timeout may have imported the file (the README says so)
checks.observed: P3 reset_failed_transient_to_pending -> 'pending' -> duplicate_check False; nothing in the code ever sets 'uncertain' after a timeout (only init --uncertain-count)

checks.what: Automation permission not granted: osascript returns -1743 'Not authorized to send Apple events to Photos' for every import
checks.method: Apple AppleScript error numbers: -1743 errAEEventNotPermitted is a global privacy setting, not a property of a file
checks.expected: non-zero exit telling the user to grant Automation access; files stay pending

checks.what: Error classifier on real AppleScript messages
checks.method: Apple error numbers: -1712 errAETimeout, -1728 errAENoSuchObject, -1743 not permitted
checks.observed: P4 -1712 photos_timeout; -1728 'osascript_busy' (it is no-such-object); -1743 permanent when the text is 'execution error: Not authorized', but transient osascript_busy when prefixed 'osascript error:'

checks.observed: Ran 93 tests in 1.26 s, OK; init/run/status/verify all execute

checks.observed: stored at resumable_photos_import.py:502, never read; MAX_TRANSIENT_ATTEMPTS = 8 hard-coded (line 58)

checks.observed: R3 'Recovered 1 interrupted file(s) to pending.' -- status resets a live worker's in-flight rows

checks.what: Sony A7R V card: verification covers every file the camera writes
checks.method: Sony A7R V writes HEIF stills as .HIF; card spec in sd_offload.py targets this camera
checks.observed: H2 manifest lists only DSC00001.ARW; DSC00002.HIF copied but never verified; errors [] -> exit 0 'safe to eject'

checks.what: Page FAQ 'Will it import the same photo twice? The manifest stops files it has already imported from being sent again ... safe after Ctrl-C or a Photos.app timeout'
checks.observed: timeout or kill then restart re-sends with duplicate check off; 'uncertain' is never set by a timeout

checks.what: Page: 'verify ... exits 1 if any is missing ... before you retire a source copy'
checks.expected: verify proves the file is in Photos
checks.observed: verify only re-reads the source files; a file falsely marked imported (R1) passes verify and its source can be retired

checks.what: Disclaimer, privacy ('no network calls, no telemetry'), served llms.txt
checks.expected: stdlib only, no network; disclaimer on page and README; clean served llms.txt
checks.observed: stdlib only (no socket/urllib); disclaimer in README and page; served copy: no placeholder or retired origin. Live host returned 000 through the proxy.

checks.what: Watchdog stall threshold vs the worker's own allowed batch time
checks.method: hand: osascript timeout = timeout*batch + 60 = 180*10+60 = 1860 s (JPEG), 600*3+60 = 1860 s (RAW), vs --stall-seconds 900
checks.observed: 900 < 1860: a slow but healthy batch is killed mid-import, which then hits the duplicate-check-off resume path

mutations.change: skip_duplicate_check = "false" if duplicate_check else "true" -> "true" (duplicate check never on)
remove the ambiguous-basename skip in bulk_preflight_pending

defects.what: Basename-only match against the whole Photos library marks a new file 'imported' without importing it whenever any older library asset shares its name (camera counters roll over); runs automatically at the start of every run and every 10 batches and after any per-item error, and the run then reports Complete. ambiguous_names only guards collisions inside the manifest.

Resume after a crash, watchdog kill or timeout re-imports with Photos duplicate detection disabled: recover_importing and reset_failed_transient_to_pending set 'pending', and 'pending' means 'skip check duplicates true'. The page promises the opposite.

Page FAQ claims no double imports and safety after Ctrl-C/timeout, and that verify gates retiring a source copy; neither is backed (verify never checks the library; timeouts never produce 'uncertain').

Automation permission denied (-1743) is classified per-file permanent: every file becomes skipped_permanent and run exits 0 'Complete'; with an 'osascript error:' prefix the same message is classified transient osascript_busy because transient patterns are checked first.
Watchdog default stall 900 s is below the worker's own osascript timeout (1860 s for 10x180 s JPEG and 3x600 s RAW), so healthy slow batches are killed mid-import.
--attempts is accepted, documented and passed by the watchdog but never used; retry limit is the hard-coded 8.
'status' calls recover_interrupted and resets a live worker's 'importing' rows to pending (then counted as interrupted).
Offload verification only covers MEDIA_EXTENSIONS; Sony .HIF (HEIF) stills from the A7R V card it targets are copied but never verified, and the run exits 0.
A successful batch osascript (rc 0) marks every file in it imported without checking the list of media items Photos returns.
No test asserts that a non-pending retry is sent with duplicate checking on: both duplicate-check mutants survive.
requirements.txt declares tenacity, which no file imports; is_retryable_status and ErrorAction.RETRY_SPLIT_BATCH are dead; read_summary in the watchdog copies ImportState.summary.
Hard-coded /Users/duncan defaults and two personal card mount points (/Volumes/Untitled 1) in shipped CLIs.

verdict: A carefully hardened resumable importer whose robustness work (atomic status files, crash-safe claims, card-unmount and wrong-disk checks, hash verification that matches sha256sum and catches a flipped byte) is real, but whose central promise, that a photo is either in Photos once or still flagged, does not hold. Run end to end with osascript mocked, a new DSC00002.JPG whose name already exists anywhere in the library is marked imported without being sent and the run reports 'Complete imported=3' (the library preflight runs on every run, not only with --photos-preflight); a file killed mid-import or timed out is re-sent after restart with 'skip check duplicates true'; denied Automation permission ends in exit 0 'Complete' with every file skipped; the watchdog's 900 s stall limit is below the worker's 1860 s batch timeout; --attempts does nothing; status mutates the manifest; Sony .HIF files are never verified. 93 tests pass in 1.3 s and caught 4 of 6 seeded bugs, but both duplicate-check mutants survive. The page's 'will not import twice' and 'verify before you retire a source copy' claims are not backed. Does not meet the bar (correctness 1, claims 1); not finished (completeness 2). Fixable in one or two sessions: recover to 'uncertain' and keep duplicate checking on for any attempts>0, make library preflight opt-in or content/date-aware, treat -1743 as a fatal run error, raise the stall default above the batch timeout, wire --attempts, make status read-only, add .hif.

evidence.correctness: Ran python3 -I /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/8c3dc66b-507d-5286-a066-00cfdd39a8bd/scratchpad/photos-import-tools/probes.py, python3 -I /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/8c3dc66b-507d-5286-a066-00cfdd39a8bd/scratchpad/photos-import-tools/probes2.py, python3 -I /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/8c3dc66b-507d-5286-a066-00cfdd39a8bd/scratchpad/photos-import-tools/probes3.py. Pass: SHA-256 equals coreutils sha256sum; one flipped byte caught by --verify hash and not by size; backoff 2..64 s and 90 s iCloud wait match the stated rules; offload exit codes 0/1/2. Fail: R1 library basename collision marks DSC00002.JPG imported without sending it and reports Complete imported=3; R4 crash-resume sends 'skip check duplicates true'; P3 timeout+restart likewise; R2 -1743 permission denied ends exit 0 Complete with 4 skipped_permanent.
evidence.completeness: Ran python3 -m unittest discover -s tests: 93 tests OK in 1.26 s. init/run/status/verify/preflight/skip-uncertain, watchdog and offload all exist and run. Gaps: --attempts never read (line 502 vs MAX_TRANSIENT_ATTEMPTS=8); status mutates the manifest (R3); 'uncertain after a timeout' described in README/page is never set by code; .HIF not verified (H2).
evidence.verification: 93 tests green; 6 mutations via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py, 4 caught (hash compare, confirmed-count boundary, watchdog remaining-work, ambiguous-name guard), 2 survived: duplicate_check any->all and forcing skip check duplicates true. Nothing tests that a retried or recovered file keeps Photos duplicate detection on, the defect that matters most here.
evidence.craft: Read resumable_photos_import.py (1,270 lines), photos_import_watchdog.py, photos_import_errors.py, sd_offload.py, atomic_io.py. Good: atomic writes, BEGIN IMMEDIATE claim, guarded OSError paths. Weak: comment essays longer than the code, read_summary duplicated from ImportState.summary, dead is_retryable_status/RETRY_SPLIT_BATCH, unused tenacity dependency, hard-coded /Users/duncan paths and personal card specs.
evidence.claims: Checked site/index.html and README against the probes. Backed: hash verification, atomic status files, non-zero exit when nothing offloaded, no network/telemetry (stdlib imports only), disclaimer on page and README, served llms.txt clean (served-copy.mjs). Not backed: 'will it import the same photo twice? ... safe after Ctrl-C or a Photos.app timeout' (R4, P3), and verify as the gate before retiring a source copy (it never checks the library, R1).
evidence.fitness: Walked the job of a photographer ingesting a 2026 card into a library holding earlier shoots: init, run (mocked osascript), verify. Files sharing a name with old library assets are silently dropped while the run says Complete and verify passes, so deleting the source after verify loses photos; a watchdog stall kill (900 s < 1860 s batch timeout) leads to duplicates. Usable only on an empty library with no interruptions.
evidence.domain: Compared to DAM ingest practice (identity by content hash or capture date+name, verify presence in the destination library before purging sources, never disable duplicate detection on an uncertain retry) and Apple's AppleScript error numbers (-1712, -1728, -1743). Departs on all three: filename identity against the whole library, duplicate check off on resume, permission errors treated per file. Card offload side (rsync --partial without --ignore-existing, SHA-256 option, wrong-disk check) is sound.
